places.name: Oia Village
places.ai_summary: A picturesque village known for its whitewashed buildings, blue-domed churches, and stunning sunset views over the Aegean Sea.

opening_hours.notes: Best visited during sunset for breathtaking views.

places.place_tip: Arrive early to secure a good spot for sunset viewing.

places.name: Akrotiri Archaeological Site
places.ai_summary: An ancient Minoan city preserved in volcanic ash, offering insights into life during the Bronze Age.
places.place_tip: Hire a guide to learn about the fascinating history of the site.

places.name: Red Beach
places.ai_summary: A unique beach with red volcanic sand and cliffs, perfect for swimming and sunbathing.

opening_hours.notes: Best visited early in the morning to avoid crowds.

places.place_tip: Bring sunscreen and water for a comfortable visit.

places.name: Santorini Caldera
places.ai_summary: A stunning volcanic caldera offering breathtaking views, hiking trails, and the famous sunset from Oia.

opening_hours.notes: Best visited during the day for hiking and sunset for views.

places.place_tip: Wear comfortable shoes for hiking and bring water.

places.name: Fira
places.ai_summary: The capital of Santorini, known for its stunning views, vibrant nightlife, and archaeological museums.

opening_hours.notes: Explore the town in the evening for a lively atmosphere.

places.place_tip: Visit the Archaeological Museum of Thera for historical insights.

places.name: Imerovigli
places.ai_summary: A charming village known for its stunning caldera views, luxury hotels, and the famous Skaros Rock.

opening_hours.notes: Best visited during sunset for romantic views.

places.place_tip: Climb Skaros Rock for panoramic views of the caldera.

attribution.title: Imerovigli 01
attribution.author: Bernard Gagnon
attribution.description: Village of Imerovigli seen from Fira, Santorini, Greece

places.name: Kamari Beach
places.ai_summary: A popular beach with black sand, crystal-clear waters, and a lively promenade with tavernas and shops.

opening_hours.notes: Great for a full day of relaxation and beach activities.

places.place_tip: Try the local seafood at beachfront tavernas.

places.name: Mykonos Windmills
places.ai_summary: Iconic windmills overlooking Mykonos town, offering panoramic views and a glimpse into the island's history.

opening_hours.notes: Best visited in the morning or late afternoon for photography.

places.place_tip: Combine your visit with a stroll around Mykonos town.

attribution.author: Mstyslav Chernov

places.name: Little Venice
places.ai_summary: A charming neighborhood with waterfront bars and restaurants, known for its picturesque sunset views.

opening_hours.notes: Best visited in the evening for a lively atmosphere.

places.place_tip: Enjoy a drink at one of the waterfront bars for a perfect sunset view.

places.name: Paros & Naxos Beaches
places.ai_summary: Beautiful beaches located on the nearby islands of Paros and Naxos, known for their crystal-clear waters and sandy shores.

opening_hours.notes: Best visited during the day for sunbathing and swimming.

places.place_tip: Take a ferry from Mykonos for a day trip to Paros and Naxos.

places.name: Rhodes Old Town
places.ai_summary: A UNESCO World Heritage site, this medieval town is famous for its well-preserved ancient ruins and vibrant street life.

opening_hours.notes: Explore the ancient ruins and enjoy the local cuisine.

places.place_tip: Visit the Palace of the Grand Master for a glimpse into the island's history.

places.name: Palace of the Grand Master of the Knights
places.ai_summary: A medieval castle located in Rhodes Old Town, offering impressive architecture and a museum.
places.place_tip: Don't miss the impressive collection of artifacts inside the palace.

places.name: Valley of the Butterflies
places.ai_summary: A beautiful natural park known for its lush greenery and thousands of butterflies that inhabit the area during the summer.

opening_hours.notes: Best visited in the morning to see the butterflies.

places.place_tip: Walk quietly to avoid scaring the butterflies.

places.name: Samaria Gorge
places.ai_summary: A stunning gorge located in the Samaria National Park, known for its dramatic scenery and hiking trails.

opening_hours.notes: Last entry at 15:00. Check weather conditions before visiting.

places.place_tip: Wear sturdy shoes and bring plenty of water.

places.name: Delos Archaeological Site
places.ai_summary: A UNESCO World Heritage site, Delos is an ancient Greek sacred island and the mythological birthplace of Apollo and Artemis.

opening_hours.notes: Last entry 30 minutes before closing. Guided tours are recommended.

places.place_tip: Bring water and snacks, as there are no facilities on the island.

places.name: Sifnos Geology
places.ai_summary: Explore the unique geological formations and stunning landscapes of Sifnos, an island less traveled by tourists.

opening_hours.notes: Best explored by hiking and walking tours.

places.place_tip: Visit the island's beaches for a complete experience of its geology.

places.name: Milos Geology
places.ai_summary: Discover the volcanic landscapes, unique rock formations, and beautiful beaches of Milos, an island with rich geological diversity.

opening_hours.notes: Best explored by car or guided tours.

places.place_tip: Don't miss the famous Sarakiniko Beach for its moon-like landscape.

places.name: Acropolis of Lindos
places.ai_summary: An ancient citadel located on a hilltop, offering stunning views and a glimpse into the ancient Greek civilization.
places.place_tip: Wear comfortable shoes for the hike up to the acropolis.

attribution.title: The Acropolis of Athens on June 1, 2021
attribution.author: George E. Koronaios
attribution.description: View of the South Slope of the Acropolis of Athens from the Hill of the Muses (Philopappos Hill). The structure on the left side of the slope is the Odeon of Herodes Atticus. It dates to the 2nd century A.D. and has a seating capacity of 5,000. The barren space on the right side of the sope is the remains of the Theatre of Dionysus. The theatre dates to the 4th cent. B.C. and had a seating capacity of 17,000.

places.name: Lindos Village
places.ai_summary: A charming village with traditional Greek architecture, narrow streets, and stunning views of the Acropolis and the sea.

opening_hours.notes: Explore the village on foot to enjoy its beauty.

places.place_tip: Visit the village's rooftop bars for a unique sunset experience.
